extracted.intended_audience: legal practitioners, solicitors, barristers, and law students (library buyers/collectors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative claims about what makes law books and practice manuals useful to practitioners and students — e.g., index quality, inclusion of statutes/forms, accuracy, practical precedents, edition/adaptation to new practice, formats and bindings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full and detailed index
rubrics_metrics.description: "That this Index is very full ... it occupies ... the same number of pages as the Act. It adduces references to the sections and sub-sections of the Act, and is prefaced by the Board of Trade memorandum."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index should be comprehensive (section/sub-section level), may include prefatory material (e.g., Board of Trade memorandum), and match the coverage of the primary statute for ease of reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of statutes, rules, fees and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Works are praised for "With the Statutes, Rules, Fees and Forms relating thereto" or "including the Acts, Rules, Forms and Costs".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical legal texts should append or embed the governing statutes, court rules, fee tables and commonly used procedural forms so they are ready for practitioner use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical precedents and common forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Books include "Precedents, Forms, and Statutes" and "Conciae Common Forms and Precedents"; collections described as "sufficiently comprehensive for ordinary use."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide ready-to-use precedents and concise common forms aimed at day-to-day drafting tasks; breadth should cover ordinary practice needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysed and considered cases (not merely listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: "the cases are not merely jotted down, but analysed and considered"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law should be explained and analysed (principles, reasoning, distinctions), not only cited, to render the information accurate and useful for practitioners and students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and completeness of content
rubrics_metrics.description: Praises such as "render the information given both accurate and complete" and "a complete treatise on the subject".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works should be thoroughly researched and aim for both factual accuracy and comprehensive topical coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation to new practice and recent legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: "adapted to the new Practice"; "written with special reference to the Acts of 1882"; "indicate substantial alterations of practice by short footnotes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatises and manuals must be updated to reflect procedural reforms and recent statutes/rules, with clear indications (e.g., footnotes, supplements) of what has changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and clarity of exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise such as "concise and careful digest", "conciseness and scientific precision", and "The principles of the law are very clearly and concisely stated."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal works should present material clearly and succinctly to be practical for quick reference and learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Useful for both practitioners and students
rubrics_metrics.description: "For Practitioners and Students"; comments like "the student will find a perusal of this epitome ... of great value" and "gives to the student a good general view."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance depth for practitioners with pedagogical features (summaries, questions, dissertations) to serve students preparing for exams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copious/discernible editorial notes and learned commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: "intelligent and learned commentary lights up ... each step"; "notes and references to the various decisions are good."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explanatory notes and learned commentary alongside precedents/cases to illuminate application and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive scope of practice coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: "as comprehensive in scope and as accurate in detail as that which so long enjoyed an almost unique reputation"; "contain the most complete list"; "a mine of information for ready reference."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference works should cover the full scope of the subject area so practitioners can rely on them as primary desk resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices with Acts, Orders, tables and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple titles note appendices: "Appendix containing Extracts from Merchant Shipping Acts...," "Appendix containing Forms and Precedents of Bills of Costs," "Appendix comprising the Order under the Solicitors' Remuneration Act, 1881, with Notes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide appendices collecting relevant statutory texts, forms, and procedural orders to supplement the main commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit treatment of procedural practice (rules, pleadings, costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Works explicitly cover practice and procedure: "Practice of the Chancery Division ... and on appeal therefrom," "Law of Costs ... with an Appendix containing Forms and Precedents of Bills of Costs," "Practice in the Queen's Bench Division ... with Statutes and Forms."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical manuals should address procedural mechanics — pleadings, costs, taxation, and rules of court — with examples and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and practical data (costs, duties, rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Tables of Costs ... Table of Stamp Duties; Legal Rate, Interest, Discount, Income, Wages and other Tables; Probate, Legacy and Succession Duties."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include up-to-date numeric tables and scales of fees/duties to allow ready calculation and compliance in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of different physical formats and bindings
rubrics_metrics.description: "kept in Stock, in law calf and other bindings"; diary issued in multiple formats (two days on a page, interleaved for attendances, whole page for each day, ruled or plain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should offer editions in practical bindings and multiple layout formats to suit different users (e.g., interleaved pages for attendance notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Edition, revision and currency indicated
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent mention of edition number and that works are "revised and adapted" or "thoroughly revised and adapted to the Conveyancing Acts".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly indicate edition/revision status and the legislative/practice date through which the work has been updated so buyers know currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elaborate/tabular indexes and tables of contents
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is an elaborate index."; "an excellent tabular Index to the County Court Acts and Rules."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed alphabetical and tabular indexes to speed location of topics and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise footnotes extracting necessary statutory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: "supplemented by concise foot notes mainly composed of extracts from statute necessary to be borne in mind by the draftsman"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise, statute-extract footnotes to highlight statutory provisions directly relevant to practical drafting and application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case digests and reported decision analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Digests described as containing "a concise analysis of every case reported" with references to text-books and consolidated digests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide case-by-case concise analyses and cross-references to authorities for rapid doctrinal research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical usefulness in judges' chambers and practitioners' offices
rubrics_metrics.description: "likely to be of material assistance to those who are much engaged in judges' chambers or in the county courts"; "of use to the Solicitor's office."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim the book's organization and contents at immediate, practical utility where decisions and forms are used daily (judges' chambers, solicitors' offices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific precision and legal drafting quality of precedents
rubrics_metrics.description: "The conciseness and scientific precision of these Precedents ... The Valuable Dissertations on the law and practice ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precedents should be drafted with technical precision and logical structure to be reliable templates for practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of recent and relevant decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: "brought down to the date of publication"; "contains the Table of Fees charged at the House of Lords"; "with references to the statutes, Rules and Orders ... to the end of 1879."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the work includes the most recent and relevant case law and statutory updates up to publication date, and identify such inclusions.
